A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DUNE, with matching core methodology, equations and experiments. All pages were readable and visually inspected. v1 ends with references; v2 adds Appendices A-C, which are available for comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification experiments on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet-100, including baseline comparisons, component ablations, parameter sensitivity and adaptive-defense evaluations.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds retrieval, computational-cost, additional-defense and perturbation-control results.

M1.justification: The shifted-label objective, spatial PGD branch, class-wise PSO color branch and ensemble optimization remain unchanged in Section 4. The new PSO pseudocode documents the existing optimizer; no altered DUNE procedure is established by the additional evaluations.

E1.justification: v2 adds Flickr8K image-to-text and text-to-image retrieval (Table 5), extending evaluation from classification to paired image-language data and retrieval tasks. CIFAR-10 and ImageNet-100 classification remain, with additional defended-input scenarios involving combined normalization or whitening and ISS-J.

E2.justification: The original 12 UE comparators remain in Table 1. v2 adds spatial-branch plus R4/R16 comparison methods (Table 9) and a clean-training reference for retrieval (Table 5). AVATAR, DVAE and ANSDA also become evaluated defenses in Table 8; their underlying works were previously only cited.

E3.justification: New evaluations introduce bidirectional retrieval measured by Hit@10 and Medr, composed channel-normalization/LAB-whitening plus ISS-J procedures, and timing measurements including 200 samples per ImageNet class. The retained classification training settings and ViT configurations are unchanged. Appendix preprocessing and optimizer settings are newly disclosed details, not evidence that existing experiments changed.

E4.justification: v2 adds targeted joint-defense tests (Table 7), robustness against three further defenses (Table 8), and Region-k controls testing whether generic low-frequency perturbations reproduce DUNE's robustness (Table 9). Computational-cost analysis is also added. The original component ablations and sensitivity/adaptive-defense plots are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report Tables 1-2 as means and standard deviations across three runs. v2 newly identifies the seeds as 0, 1025 and 2025; it does not state an increase in runs or introduce a new statistical testing procedure.

E6.justification: Tables 1-3 and the original ablation table, renumbered from Table 4 to Table 6, retain identical values. v2 adds results in Tables 4-5 and 7-9, including image-to-text Hit@10 of 13.9 for DUNE versus 22.7 for clean training, and ResNet18 accuracy of 67.97±0.87 under channel normalization plus ISS-J. These are newly reported conditions, not improvements on retained tests.

T1.justification: The mathematical objectives, constraints and adaptive-defense formulations in Equations 1-20 are retained. No theorem, proof or substantive derivation is added. The PSO listing supplies implementation details rather than new theoretical analysis.

C1.justification: The abstract slightly narrows its criticism from existing UE schemes to certain existing UE schemes. The central dual-domain and ensemble contributions, and the headline comparison against 12 UE methods under seven defenses, remain unchanged; the added experiments primarily supply further evidence.

C2.justification: Remark I and Section 5.5 add explanations involving coupled cross-domain and representation-level biases. Appendix B interprets the Region-k controls as distinguishing luminance-oriented color perturbations from generic low-frequency noise, while Section 5.4 adds an explanation of ensemble-size sensitivity. These refine the existing robustness interpretation.

D1.justification: Appendix A newly specifies quality thresholds, PSO initialization and update rules, ten particles and ten iterations, checkpoint provenance, 224x224 ImageNet crops and training augmentation. Section 5.2 adds timing and FLOP information, and Appendices B-C clarify implementation sources. The full DUNE pseudocode is removed and replaced by a PSO-only listing; the code-access link remains unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds UE-related works by Cai et al. (2026) and Li et al. (2026a,b), while removing several backdoor, transformer and iterative-filtering references and the explicit backdoor analogy. The overall positioning against heuristic and single-domain UEs remains. Publication updates for existing references do not constitute new works.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most prose remain intact. Changes include localized explanatory revisions, a shortened impact statement, updated affiliations and correspondence information, acknowledgements, and new appendix subsections. This is not an extensive rewrite of the existing narrative.

P2.justification: v2 adds five tables covering runtime, retrieval, joint defenses, additional defenses and Region-k controls, and rearranges the experimental displays. The full DUNE algorithm display is replaced by a different PSO-only appendix listing. Figure 5 explicitly labels PGD and PSO, and Figure 3 gains an explanation of its parameter-space directions.

improvement.justification: The joint-defense and Region-k experiments strengthen evidence for the retained robustness argument, while Appendix A supplies useful missing optimization settings. However, the retrieval model, splits and adaptation procedure remain unspecified, and the complete DUNE pseudocode is removed. The runtime summary also leaves its below-one/below-eight-hour claims unreconciled with branch times summing to approximately 1.30/8.94 hours in Table 4. These limitations constrain the otherwise positive gains in evidence and reproducibility.
